episodes.166738: A cold front produced scattered thunderstorms that resulted in several gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.167373: With an upper trough moving over the area from the north, downpours occurred from the Big Island to Kauai.  The precipitation caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.167463: A series of upper-level disturbances shifting over a moderately unstable environment near a weak surface boundary led to thunderstorms capable of producing hail.
episodes.167583: A cold front stalled across the Mid-South. This was the focus for thunderstorms that produced large hail on Easter Sunday.
episodes.167742: A stationary front extended from west to east along the I-20 corridor of East Texas and North Louisiana around daybreak on April 17th, which slowly lifted back north into Northeast Texas and Southern Arkansas through the afternoon. Meanwhile, an upper level trough dove southeast through the Southern Plains during the day, reinforcing a cold front southeast across the region. These features enhanced large scale ascent as they interacted with a warm, moist, and unstable air mass that had begun to surge back to the north. As a result, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and spread east-northeast from late morning through the afternoon across Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana. An isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Titus County Texas, producing large hail near the Winfield community before shifting off to the east into Southwest Arkansas and North Louisiana through the afternoon.
episodes.167744: A stationary front extended from west to east along the I-20 corridor of East Texas and North Louisiana around daybreak on April 17th, which slowly lifted back north into Northeast Texas and Southern Arkansas through the afternoon. Meanwhile, an upper level trough dove southeast through the Southern Plains during the day, reinforcing a cold front southeast across the region. These features enhanced large scale ascent as they interacted with a warm, moist, and unstable air mass that had begun to surge back to the north. As a result, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and spread east-northeast from late morning through the afternoon across Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana. An isolated severe thunderstorm developed a couple miles northeast of Ruston in Southeast Lincoln Parish, producing large hail before weakening as it moved into Northern Jackson and Western Ouachita Parish.
episodes.168026: An approaching cold front brought a couple of rounds of showers and thunderstorms to the tri-state region.  Severe weather was confined to southeast Alabama and the Florida panhandle with lower instability further east into southern Georgia and the Florida big bend.
episodes.168027: An approaching cold front brought a couple of rounds of showers and thunderstorms to the tri-state region.  Severe weather was confined to southeast Alabama and the Florida panhandle with lower instability further east into southern Georgia and the Florida big bend.
episodes.168299: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Ouachita River and Black River in mid April.
episodes.168308: Stationary boundary across the I-10 corridor lifted northward as a warm front on Easter day. Behind the front, substantial surface heating, cold temperatures aloft, and an unstable air mass resulted in strong to severe thunderstorms developing along the inland moving sea breezes for portions of northeast FL in the afternoon.  Severe thunderstorms produced large hail up to 2 inches in the vicinity of Nocatee and Palm Valley in northern St. Johns County and Palm Coast in Flagler County along the active Atlantic sea breeze boundary. A severe thunderstorm also downed several trees in Ocala due to a mircoburst.
episodes.168506: With a front positioned along the Missouri border, a few strong storms developed and moved along it during the evening hours April 15th leading to reports of large hail and wind damage. Additional storms developed across eastern Oklahoma later that night into the 16th  and moved southeastward across potions of western and southern Arkansas. Large hail was the most common severe weather report, with some spotty wind damage occurring as well.||The cold front that moved through on the 13th (bringing cooler air/a temporary end to active weather) was headed back into the state from the Gulf Coast. The front was the focus for a massive storm toward the Missouri border in the evening. Between 700 pm and 1000 pm CDT, the storm tracked east/southeast along the front through Baxter, Fulton, Sharp, Lawrence, Greene, Craighead, and Mississippi Counties. Along the way, the storm unleashed huge hail that damaged structures and vehicles. Hail was softball size or larger at Cherokee Village (Sharp County) and five miles west of Viola (Fulton County). ||The radar detected strong rotation in the storm, and there were indications the storm may be tornadic. Several Tornado Warnings were issued, and Tornado Emergencies were declared given damage reports and sightings of funnels reaching the ground. However, it appears most of the damage was caused by hail, and there were no confirmations of tornadoes during a damage survey.||Early on the 16th, a new cold front approached from the northwest, and triggered more storms across the western counties. Before 700 am CDT, trees and powerlines were downed at Waldron (Scott County), and two to three inches of rain was measured. A barn was damaged, a tree was blown onto a house, and there was golf ball size hail at Oden (Montgomery County). More trees were toppled at Mount Ida (Montgomery County), and the west side of town lost power. Rain came down in buckets, with 1.59 inches of precipitation in only 23 minutes! A tree fell on a car at Silver (Montgomery County), and quarter size hail was reported at Bismarck (Hot Spring County) and Caulksville (Logan County).
episodes.168519: Thunderstorms developed in the warm, moist airmass ahead of cold front and moved through South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.168756: A mesoscale convective system was racing south to southwestward across Mississippi and Alabama midday on April 16th. Southerly winds ahead of this system aided to transport warm and moist air into it. A partial acceleration of the leading edge of the MCS resulted in severe winds over Ship Island.
episodes.169120: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the mid-Atlantic ahead of a cold front on April 16. The storms developed in an environment of little to no surface based instability. However, some elevated instability and cold air aloft, combined with strong frontal forcing, allowed storms to develop. Thanks to the steep lapse rates aloft, several storms produced hail. Hail was mainly sub-severe in nature, but a couple reports of hail close to one inch in diameter were received. Showers and storms moved off the coast by later in the evening of the 16th.

episodes.174378: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms produced large hail, damaging wind gusts, and tornadoes through the day on April 17th.
episodes.177386: A line of thunderstorms moved through central and northeast Louisiana on the afternoon of April 17th and produced wind damage in the area.

An up to two mile wide swath of straight-line wind damage associated with the rear flank downdraft of a thunderstorm occurred through the D'Lo and Mendenhall areas of Simpson County. Residents in the area described an approximately 5 minute period of high winds and heavy rain as the storm pushed through. Several large trees were uprooted and snapped in the swath, and a few were snapped at the trunk. Several trees fell onto homes and power lines. A few trees fell onto an apartment complex in Mendenhall, with the roof sustaining damage. A service station canopy along US Highway 49 collapsed into the pumps and convenience store. In the corridor of strongest winds which occurred on the north side of downtown Mendenhall, wind gusts were estimated to be near 90 MPH, with tree damage observed on most streets in that area.
